codeReview.summary: The slice adds the `flux profile create|list|use|delete` surface and persists saved per-profile state, but profile switching still does not isolate the full effective state when the CLI starts from environment-backed auth, enterprise-key, FluxDrive, or HTTP defaults. In those configured sessions, `profile list`/`state show` report one bundle while `flux_get_state` keeps using another shared bundle across profiles.

issues.description: `hydratePersistedSessionState()` only reapplies persisted `zelidauth`, `enterpriseKey`, FluxDrive base URL, and HTTP defaults when the selected profile has explicit non-null/non-default values (`fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:848-885`). New/default profile state, however, is seeded with only `FLUX_API_BASE_URL` and hard-coded defaults (`fluxos-cli/src/state/sessionState.ts:95-105`), while the real MCP runtime still bootstraps auth, enterprise-key, FluxDrive, and HTTP defaults from `FLUX_ZELIDAUTH`, `FLUX_ENTERPRISE_KEY`, `FLUXDRIVE_MWS_BASE_URL`, and `FLUX_HTTP_*` (`flux-mcp/src/index.ts:116-119`, `:2059-2062`; `flux-mcp/src/fluxClient.ts:168-174`). In practice, two fresh profiles both show `auth.present: false`, `enterpriseKey.present: false`, default FluxDrive, and default HTTP settings in `profile list` / `state show`, yet `flux tool call flux_get_state --json` still reports the same env-backed auth, enterprise key, FluxDrive URL, and HTTP defaults under both profiles. That breaks VAL-PROFILE-002 / VAL-CROSS-002 because profile switches do not restore an isolated coherent state bundle, and the JSON visibility contract is misleading in configured environments.

summary: Fail. The new profile commands work for purely persisted state, but per-profile isolation is not actually enforced for env-backed auth, enterprise-key, FluxDrive, and HTTP-default state, so switching profiles can still leave a shared effective configuration.
